clue.text: Female regularly blushes after answer is wrong

indicators.note: the regular letters come after the answer's abbreviation in the build
regularly picks every other letter of blushes, here the even ones

parts.note: its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters

explanation.surface: A woman goes red after giving an answer that turns out to be incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue or incorrect is wrong; 'is wrong' reads as the adjective with its verb.

clue.text: Great carbonated drink — it's turned up cold!

parts.note: Fanta is a brand of fizzy orange drink

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: the letters of it's, without the apostrophe
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fizzy drink that has been served chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic and great are both informal words of high praise, meaning excellent.

clue.text: Daisy, perhaps, not the first cow

indicators.note: says the first letter of the flower is dropped

parts.note: a daisy is an example of a flower

explanation.surface: Daisy is a typical name for a cow, so she might seem not the leading one in the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy reads as a cow's name, but it is the flower; 'cow' is the definition, as a cow is something that lows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow moos, or lows, so in crossword humour it is one that lows; also a verb meaning to frown.

clue.text: Fee from ten writers in eastern Spain

indicators.note: the numeral and the pens are placed inside the two single letters

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
X is the Roman numeral for ten
pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: A charge is levied on ten authors in the east of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cost or charge that must be paid out is an outlay, like a fee.

clue.text: Fill up net at sea, overflowing

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fisherman fills his net while out on the water until it spills over.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply that is abundant to the point of excess can be called overflowing.

clue.text: Little dog, favourite poodle

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A small dog, a beloved poodle, sounds like a family's darling.
explanation.walkthrough: Poodle looks like the breed in a list of dogs; it is slang for a servile follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle, in political slang, is a lackey controlled by another, just like a marionette.

clue.text: Working on a puree? Swede, maybe

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Mashing a swede, the root vegetable, into a puree in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A swede is a root vegetable (a rutabaga) that is often pureed; here it is a person from Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, so an example of someone from the continent.

clue.text: Little swimmer's time on pedalo wound up

indicators.note: wound up as in twisted round, so the letters of the boat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's turn on a pedal boat comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay; a pedalo is a small pedal-powered pleasure boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog's larva is a small aquatic creature that swims with its tail.

clue.text: Lucky for fish the hook's first removed

parts.note: tuna is a fish

indicators.note: removed means that letter is taken out of the word the
first picks the opening letter of hook

parts.note: the first letter of hook

explanation.surface: An angler is lucky that the fish got free of the hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lucky and being fortunate both mean blessed by good luck.

clue.text: House deposit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to house someone is to give them lodging
second meaning: to deposit something is to place it with someone, as in lodging a complaint

explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to lodge is both to accommodate a person and to place or file something formally.

clue.text: Pans we moved with a rag

indicators.note: moved means the letters of 'pans we' are shifted into a new order

parts.note: a, as in 'five pounds a head', means per

explanation.surface: Someone shifts cooking pans around and wipes them with a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' looks like a cleaning cloth in the kitchen scene; it is slang for a poor-quality paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive slang term for a low-quality daily paper or tabloid.

clue.text: Challenged father over religious education

indicators.note: father is spread over the subject, covering it on both sides

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A parent objects to what their child is taught in religion lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To have challenged someone to do something is to have dared them.

clue.text: Tidy area right beside stove

parts.note: a range is a large cooking stove

explanation.surface: Someone tidies the kitchen area to the right of the cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy things is to put them in order, to set them out neatly.

clue.text: Stuff that's made for Mussolini?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
Mussolini styled himself Il Duce, the leader

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what manufactured goods might be called if you supported Italy's dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: being 'for' the Duce splits the word as a supporter of Mussolini.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods grown or manufactured, especially farm goods, are collectively called this noun.

clue.text: Drunkard pinching papa's hat

indicators.note: the drinker pinches, i.e. grips, the letter between its own

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker
papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's links it to the hat

explanation.surface: A drunk steals his father's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is called this informally, a tall formal piece of headwear.

clue.text: Philosopher almost makes passengers wait on these?

indicators.note: almost means the philosopher's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Plato was the Greek philosopher
forms means makes, creates

explanation.surface: A thinker nearly creates the places where travellers stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Plato's theory of Forms adds a nice touch to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: At a railway station, travellers stand on raised areas beside the track waiting for trains.

clue.text: Found everyone following British game

parts.note: to found something is to base it

indicators.note: following puts everyone's word after British's letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that the whole team followed a British sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts ALL after B. 'Found' reads as the past of find but is the verb to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an American bat-and-ball sport, so an example of a game.

clue.text: Make-up stays on cheek? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts one piece below another
says the order is the other way round: cheek on top of stays

parts.note: lip is cheek, insolence
sticks means stays put

explanation.surface: A cosmetic stays put on the cheek, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays on cheek' would give STICKS under LIP the wrong way; 'On the contrary' flips it so the cheek word goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured cosmetics for the mouth are a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Gloomy conductor might indicate this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pessimistic, low in mood
second meaning: the first beat of a bar, shown by a conductor's downward stroke

explanation.walkthrough: A gloomy conductor sounds like one person; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pessimistic in mood and also the accented first beat a conductor marks with a downward baton.

clue.text: Defend prisoner swallowing meat pie nearly

indicators.note: the prisoner swallows, taking the other letters inside

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
ham is a meat

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of pie, dropping its last letter

parts.note: the word pie, cut short

explanation.surface: A prisoner wolfs down most of a meat pie and has to stick up for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause or person is to support and stand up for them, as a verb.

clue.text: Demonstration from professional ahead of cricket match?

indicators.note: in a down answer, ahead of means placed above, so first

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A professional player stages a demonstration before an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A public demonstration is a march or rally voicing objection.

clue.text: Martial artist bitten by snake becomes numb

indicators.note: the snake's jaws close round the artist, so his name goes inside

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Bruce Lee was the famous martial artist

explanation.surface: A kung fu fighter is bitten by a snake and his limbs lose feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone dead, with pins and needles, is said to have fallen into this state.

clue.text: Cakes son smells around rear of bakehouse

indicators.note: the smells go around the letter

parts.note: pongs are smells; pong is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: rear of means the last letter

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A boy sniffs cakes near the back of a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: Light sponge cakes are airy cakes made from eggs, flour and sugar.

clue.text: Quietly studied after second meal

indicators.note: after places the quiet-and-studied pieces behind the second's letter

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Someone read silently after eating their next course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts P and READ after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish meal or feast laid out on a table is a spread.

clue.text: Lover with nothing on — one fools around

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or lover of something, as in film buff
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A naked lover is someone who messes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover with nothing on' suggests 'in the buff', naked, a nice extra touch; but BUFF is the enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown or joker is someone who fools around.

clue.text: New English Bible initially turned up on church pew

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from the bottom, i.e. backwards
initially picks the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A New English Bible was found lying on a church pew.
explanation.walkthrough: Initial letters give NEB, which turned up becomes BEN; 'on' places CH below it in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pew is a long seat in church, a type of long seat for several people.

clue.text: Take care of scheme after change of heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the scheme word is swapped for another letter

parts.note: a project is a planned scheme

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a plan after altering their opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of PROJECT is its middle letter J; changing it to T gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone safe from harm is to look after them.

clue.text: School, we're told, is demolished

indicators.note: we're told means heard, the school's name said aloud

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: We hear that a school has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: Demolished sounds like building work, but it means devoured, as food is.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been demolished has been wolfed down, consumed completely.

clue.text: Thinner vegetable absorbs sauce

indicators.note: the two words soak up the answer, holding it within their letters

explanation.surface: A slimmer vegetable soaks up the gravy on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks like gravy in the kitchen surface; here it means cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce, like nerve, means impudence or cheek, as in 'what a nerve'.

clue.text: Touring Greece with tin full of beans

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller goes round Greece with a can of beans in their pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of beans is an idiom for lively and bursting with vigour.

clue.text: Spoke about India after the man paused

indicators.note: the speech word comes after the pronoun

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man

indicators.note: the spoken word goes about, around the letter

parts.note: spoke here means stated, said
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man talked about India, then fell silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To have paused uncertainly before acting or speaking is to have wavered.

clue.text: Drops from dark liquid found in ship

indicators.note: found in places the liquid inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
ink is a dark writing liquid

explanation.surface: Drips of an inky fluid turn up aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like a noun, drips of liquid, but it is the verb to go down.
explanation.definitionFit: To descend or go down in level is to fall, as a ship does when it goes under.
